page: Microsoft Azure E8bs_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Driven by dedicated Intel processors, the instance delivers 8 vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of system RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core resource distribution. The configuration contains no discrete graphics hardware accelerators, operating with zero onboard GPUs.

A key engineering focus of the Ebs_v6 family is block storage performance, including support for Premium Storage. The E8bs_v6 does not provision local ephemeral storage disks, which requires all operating system partitions, cache tiers, and persistent data directories to rely on network-attached block volumes. Furthermore, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network integration for direct external routing.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-core ratio allows organizations to scale working memory without over-provisioning compute threads. The trade-off centers on the complete absence of local disk drives, ensuring operational consistency via decoupled block storage while avoiding the retention risks of node-local storage.

The E8bs_v6 is structured to support workloads that depend on substantial memory allocations alongside dependable remote disk I/O throughput. Representative target environments include relational databases, in-memory data structures, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and memory-constrained enterprise application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure E8bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Driven by dedicated x86_64 Intel processor hardware, the configuration delivers 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance does not feature local disk storage or onboard GPUs, relying entirely on remote Premium Storage-capable block volumes for operating systems, application binaries, and persistent datasets. Network routing relies on separately provisioned endpoints, as no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance. Tailored for memory-centric operational environments, the E8bs_v6 offers strong memory capacity per processing thread, minimizing the risk of memory saturation in demanding data workloads. This architectural balance makes the instance appropriate for medium-scale relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, enterprise data warehousing tasks, and memory-intensive transactional backend services.
